metrics.label: RSRP
metrics.whatItMeasures: Reference Signal Received Power — the strength of the cellular signal from the tower to your phone.
metrics.currentValueContext: Measured in dBm (decibel-milliwatts). Higher (less negative) = stronger signal.
metrics.healthyRange: -80 dBm to -100 dBm is good. Below -120 dBm is very weak.
metrics.commonCauses: Thick walls, basement, distance from tower, building materials, network congestion.

metrics.label: RSRQ
metrics.whatItMeasures: Reference Signal Received Quality — the quality of the received signal, factoring in interference and noise.
metrics.currentValueContext: Measured in dB. Higher (less negative) = better quality.
metrics.healthyRange: -5 dB to -10 dB is good. Below -15 dB indicates significant interference.
metrics.commonCauses: Network congestion, interference from other cell towers, physical obstructions causing signal reflections.

metrics.label: SINR
metrics.whatItMeasures: Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio — how clean your signal is versus background noise and interference.
metrics.currentValueContext: Measured in dB. Higher = cleaner signal. This is the best indicator of actual data performance. '--' means the radio reports no measurable value right now (not a bad signal — often just idle), or a physically impossible reading was rejected. Valid real-world range is -23 dB to +40 dB.
metrics.healthyRange: 13 dB+ is excellent. 5-13 dB is good. Below 5 dB means poor conditions. A displayed value below -23 dB or above +40 dB is an invalid/placeholder reading, not a real measurement.
metrics.commonCauses: Edge of cell coverage, interference from other towers, building materials, many users on the same tower. Some phone models (e.g. certain OPPO/OnePlus builds) only expose SINR via the consolidated signal-strength API, so it may be unavailable while that path is quiet.
metrics.expansion: SIGNAL TO INTERFERENCE PLUS NOISE RATIO

metrics.label: Active Band
metrics.whatItMeasures: A band is a licensed slice of the radio spectrum a carrier uses for cellular service — a reserved "lane" on the airwaves. 3GPP numbers each one (B3, n78…): B = 4G LTE, n = 5G NR. This shows the band your phone is actively camped on.
metrics.currentValueContext: The core trade-off is physics: lower frequencies travel further and penetrate walls better but carry less data; higher frequencies are faster but shorter-range and easily blocked. Low-band (<1 GHz — B12/B20/B71, n28/n71): the coverage “safety net” — long range and solid indoors, modest speeds. Mid-band (1–6 GHz — B1/B3/B7/B41, n41/n77/n78): the everyday workhorse — wide-area coverage with genuinely fast speeds; n78 (~3.5 GHz) is the global mid-band 5G standard. High-band mmWave (24–71 GHz — n257/n258/n260): multi-Gbps bursts, but line-of-sight only — expect it at malls, stadiums and dense urban streets, not at home.
metrics.healthyRange: Any connected band is normal. Expect low-band to feel slower, mid-band to be the typical fast experience, and mmWave to be very fast but rare. Switching between bands is the phone adapting to coverage and congestion — not a fault.
metrics.commonCauses: Your carrier decides which bands are deployed in your area and which your phone may camp on. The phone selects bands automatically from signal strength, network load and carrier-aggregation state, and re-selects as you move.

metrics.label: IMS Registration
metrics.whatItMeasures: IP Multimedia Subsystem registration — whether your phone can use VoLTE (voice over 4G/5G) and WiFi Calling.
metrics.currentValueContext: When registered, calls use data networks. When not registered, calls fall back to older 2G/3G networks.
metrics.healthyRange: Registered = good. Not registered = calls may drop or fail.
metrics.commonCauses: Carrier provisioning issue, incorrect APN settings, roaming on a network that doesn't support your IMS profile, software bug.

metrics.label: Network Type
metrics.whatItMeasures: The generation and type of cellular network your phone is currently using for data.
metrics.currentValueContext: NR = 5G, LTE = 4G, HSPA = 3G, EDGE/GPRS = 2G. Faster generations deliver better speeds.
metrics.healthyRange: NR or LTE is normal for modern smartphones.
metrics.commonCauses: Network coverage area, carrier settings, phone capabilities, network congestion, data saver mode.

metrics.label: Roaming
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether your phone is connected to a network other than your primary carrier's home network.
metrics.currentValueContext: On = you're using another carrier's network. May incur extra charges depending on your plan.
metrics.healthyRange: Off is normal when not travelling. On is expected when abroad or in areas without your carrier's coverage.
metrics.commonCauses: International travel, remote area with no home carrier coverage, network outage on your carrier.

metrics.label: Cell ID (eCID)
metrics.whatItMeasures: A unique identifier for the specific cell tower sector your phone is connected to.
metrics.currentValueContext: This number identifies which physical tower you're connected to. Useful for tracking coverage patterns.
metrics.healthyRange: Any value is normal. Frequent changes mean you're moving or the network is handing you off between towers.
metrics.commonCauses: Walking or driving between cell coverage areas, network load balancing.

metrics.label: Battery Level
metrics.whatItMeasures: The current charge level of your phone's battery as a percentage of its capacity.
metrics.currentValueContext: 0% = empty, 100% = full charge. Below 20% most phones enter low-power mode.
metrics.healthyRange: 20-100% is normal operating range.
metrics.commonCauses: Usage patterns, screen brightness, background processes, cellular signal strength (weak signal drains more), battery age.

metrics.label: Battery Health
metrics.whatItMeasures: The physical condition of your battery as reported by the built-in fuel gauge chip.
metrics.currentValueContext: Good = normal. Overheat = too hot, may limit charging. Dead = needs replacement. Cold = below operating temperature.
metrics.healthyRange: Good is the only normal reading for a healthy battery.
metrics.commonCauses: Battery age (lithium batteries degrade after 2-3 years), physical damage, extreme temperatures, manufacturing defect.

metrics.label: Charge Rate
metrics.whatItMeasures: How fast your battery is currently charging or discharging, in microamps.
metrics.currentValueContext: Positive = charging. Negative = discharging. Zero = not connected to power and not draining.
metrics.healthyRange: Charging: 1,000,000-3,000,000 µA is typical. Discharging: -100,000 to -500,000 µA is normal screen-on drain.
metrics.commonCauses: Charger speed, cable quality, battery temperature (charging slows when hot), background activity.

metrics.label: Power Consumption by App
metrics.whatItMeasures: Estimated power draw attributed to each running app and system process.
metrics.currentValueContext: Higher values mean that app is draining more battery. Based on estimated power profiles, not direct measurement.
metrics.healthyRange: Screen usually consumes 30-50% of total. Background apps should be under 5% each.
metrics.commonCauses: App actively doing work, background sync, location services, poor network causing retries, buggy app keeping CPU awake.

metrics.label: CPU Load
metrics.whatItMeasures: How busy each CPU core is, as a percentage of its maximum capacity.
metrics.currentValueContext: 0.0 = idle. 1.0 = completely busy. Most phones have 8 cores (4 efficiency + 4 performance).
metrics.healthyRange: Idle: under 0.1 per core. Normal usage: 0.2-0.5. Heavy gaming/editing: 0.8-1.0.
metrics.commonCauses: Running apps, background processes, system updates, malware, thermal throttling reducing max speed.

metrics.label: Memory Pressure
metrics.whatItMeasures: How constrained the system is by available RAM. High pressure means apps will be killed to free memory.
metrics.currentValueContext: Normal = plenty of RAM. Moderate = system is starting to reclaim memory. Critical = apps are being killed.
metrics.healthyRange: Normal is best. Brief Moderate is OK. Critical means you should close some apps.
metrics.commonCauses: Too many apps running, memory leak in an app, very large app (game or editor), outdated phone with limited RAM.

metrics.label: Storage Used
metrics.whatItMeasures: How much of your internal storage is occupied by apps, media, system files, and cached data.
metrics.currentValueContext: Shown as used vs total. Also broken down by system vs user data for clarity.
metrics.healthyRange: Under 80% full is comfortable. Above 90% the system may slow down. Above 95% you'll get warnings.
metrics.commonCauses: Photos and videos, large games, cached streaming data, downloaded content, system updates.

metrics.label: SIM Provisioning
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether your SIM or eSIM is activated and ready for service on your carrier's network.
metrics.currentValueContext: Provisioned = ready to use. Not provisioned = SIM may not be activated with your carrier.
metrics.healthyRange: Provisioned is the only normal state for active service.
metrics.commonCauses: New SIM not yet activated, eSIM download incomplete, carrier provisioning delay, SIM card failure.

metrics.label: eSIM Profiles
metrics.whatItMeasures: The number of eSIM profiles installed on your device. Each profile represents a carrier subscription.
metrics.currentValueContext: One profile per active eSIM line. Multiple profiles can be installed but only two (usually) active at once.
metrics.healthyRange: 1-2 profiles is typical. Power users may have 3-5 for travel.
metrics.commonCauses: Adding travel eSIMs, switching carriers, work/personal dual-SIM setup, left old profiles installed.

metrics.label: IP Address
metrics.whatItMeasures: Your device's current IP address on the network — unique identifier for sending and receiving data.
metrics.currentValueContext: IPv4 shown as four numbers separated by dots. IPv6 shown as hexadecimal. Multiple addresses means multiple network interfaces.
metrics.healthyRange: Any valid IP address is normal. If no IP is shown, you're not connected to any network.
metrics.commonCauses: DHCP assignment from router, carrier-assigned IP for mobile data, VPN assigning a new IP, IP address conflict.

metrics.label: Active Network
metrics.whatItMeasures: Which network interface your phone is currently using for internet traffic.
metrics.currentValueContext: WiFi = connected to a wireless network. Mobile = using cellular data. VPN = all traffic going through VPN tunnel.
metrics.healthyRange: Any is normal. WiFi is usually faster and uses less battery than mobile data.
metrics.commonCauses: WiFi range, mobile data enabled, VPN app active, airplane mode, hotspot/tethering active.

metrics.label: Temperature
metrics.whatItMeasures: The temperature of various components inside your phone — CPU, battery, modem, and others.
metrics.currentValueContext: Multiple zones monitored independently. The hottest zone typically determines whether the phone throttles.
metrics.healthyRange: Under 40°C is cool. 40-55°C is warm. Above 55°C may trigger throttling to protect components.
metrics.commonCauses: Heavy gaming or video, direct sunlight, fast charging, poor case ventilation, faulty battery.

metrics.label: Throttling
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether the system is intentionally reducing performance to lower temperature and protect components.
metrics.currentValueContext: Active = phone is hot and performance is being reduced. Inactive = everything is normal.
metrics.healthyRange: Inactive is ideal. Brief throttling during heavy use is normal. Constant throttling suggests a problem.
metrics.commonCauses: High ambient temperature, sustained heavy load (gaming, video recording), blocked ventilation, case trapping heat.

metrics.label: Kernel Version
metrics.whatItMeasures: The version of the Linux kernel your Android OS is running on — the core bridge between software and hardware.
metrics.currentValueContext: This is the version string reported by the OS. Newer kernels have better security and hardware support.
metrics.healthyRange: Any officially supported version from your device manufacturer is normal.
metrics.commonCauses: Android OS updates, custom ROM installation, carrier-mandated kernel versions.

metrics.label: SELinux Status
metrics.whatItMeasures: Security-Enhanced Linux — Android's mandatory access control system. Enforced means security policies are active.
metrics.currentValueContext: Enforced = security policies active. Permissive = policies log but don't block (less secure).
metrics.healthyRange: Enforced is normal for production devices.
metrics.commonCauses: Custom ROMs may set permissive for compatibility. Some rooting methods disable SELinux enforcement.

metrics.label: Uptime
metrics.whatItMeasures: How long it's been since your phone was last restarted or powered on.
metrics.currentValueContext: Longer uptime means the phone hasn't had a fresh start recently. Good for stability, but occasional reboots help clear accumulated state.
metrics.healthyRange: Days to weeks is normal. Months without reboot may indicate OS updates are being skipped.
metrics.commonCauses: No recent restart, OS update pending, good stability, or significant uptime (user habit).

metrics.label: Kernel Wakelocks
metrics.whatItMeasures: System-level locks that prevent the phone from entering deep sleep. Each wakelock keeps some part of the hardware awake.
metrics.currentValueContext: Power Mode only. Each entry shows what's holding the phone awake and for how long. More wakelocks = more battery drain.
metrics.healthyRange: A few seconds per minute is normal. Multiple minutes of wake time means something is preventing sleep.
metrics.commonCauses: Apps with background services, push notifications, music playback, navigation, buggy apps not releasing wakelocks.

metrics.label: Hotspot Power Overhead
metrics.whatItMeasures: The additional power drain caused by using your phone as a WiFi hotspot or mobile tethering.
metrics.currentValueContext: Shown as estimated additional draw compared to normal usage without hotspot active.
metrics.healthyRange: Minimal when idle. Adds significant drain when actively passing data to connected devices.
metrics.commonCauses: Connected devices actively using internet, background sync on connected devices, poor cellular signal (hotspot uses more power to maintain connection).

metrics.label: Home PLMN (MCC-MNC)
metrics.whatItMeasures: The Public Land Mobile Network identity of your home carrier — a combination of your country code (MCC) and carrier code (MNC).
metrics.currentValueContext: First 3 digits = country (MCC), next 2-3 = carrier (MNC). This is read directly from your SIM card.
metrics.healthyRange: Should match your carrier's assigned MCC-MNC. Mismatch may indicate wrong SIM or a compromised device.
metrics.commonCauses: Different carrier SIM inserted, roaming partner SIM, MVNO using host carrier's MNC.

metrics.label: Network PLMN (Serving)
metrics.whatItMeasures: The MCC-MNC of the cellular network your phone is currently connected to for service.
metrics.currentValueContext: This is the PLMN broadcast by the tower you're camped on. May differ from your home PLMN when roaming.
metrics.healthyRange: Should match home PLMN when not roaming. Different PLMN = roaming on another carrier's network.
metrics.commonCauses: Roaming internationally, using a secondary carrier's network due to weak home signal, network sharing agreement.

metrics.label: Call State
metrics.whatItMeasures: The current state of voice calling on your device — idle, ringing, or in a call.
metrics.currentValueContext: IDLE = no call activity. RINGING = incoming call. OFFHOOK = call in progress.
metrics.healthyRange: IDLE is normal when not on a call. OFFHOOK is normal during calls.
metrics.commonCauses: Incoming/outgoing calls, call waiting, dialing a number.

metrics.label: Radio Power State
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether the cellular radio (modem) is powered on, off, or in an unavailable state.
metrics.currentValueContext: ON = radio is active (normal). OFF = radio powered down (airplane mode). UNAVAILABLE = cannot determine.
metrics.healthyRange: ON is the only normal state for active cellular service.
metrics.commonCauses: Airplane mode, system crash causing modem restart, radio firmware issue, battery saver turning off radio.

metrics.label: IMS Capable
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether your carrier and device support IP Multimedia Subsystem — required for VoLTE, WiFi Calling, and RCS.
metrics.currentValueContext: Read from the carrier's configuration database. YES = IMS features are provisioned.
metrics.healthyRange: YES is normal for modern smartphones with VoLTE service.
metrics.commonCauses: Carrier provisioning, device firmware support, MVNO without IMS agreement, outdated carrier settings.

metrics.label: VoLTE
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether Voice over LTE (VoLTE) is enabled on your device — allowing high-quality voice calls over the 4G/5G data connection.
metrics.currentValueContext: ENABLED = your calls will use VoLTE. DISABLED = calls fall back to older networks.
metrics.healthyRange: ENABLED provides better call quality and faster call setup.
metrics.commonCauses: Carrier provisioning, device VoLTE toggle, IMS registration status, network compatibility.

metrics.label: WiFi Calling
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether WiFi Calling is available and active on your device — allowing calls over WiFi when cellular signal is weak.
metrics.currentValueContext: READY = enabled and available. ACTIVE = currently using WiFi for calls. UNAVAILABLE = not available.
metrics.healthyRange: READY or ACTIVE is normal for supported carriers.
metrics.commonCauses: Carrier support, WiFi connection quality, E911 address registration required, IMS registration status.

metrics.label: NR-NSA (EN-DC)
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether your carrier supports Non-Standalone 5G (also called EN-DC) — 5G that uses LTE as an anchor.
metrics.currentValueContext: YES = carrier config supports NR-NSA. This is the most common 5G deployment today.
metrics.healthyRange: YES is normal for 5G-capable devices on carriers that offer 5G.
metrics.commonCauses: Carrier 5G deployment strategy, device firmware, plan provisioning, network coverage area.

metrics.label: Preferred Network Type
metrics.whatItMeasures: The network modes your device is configured to prefer — e.g., 5G/LTE only, or auto-switching between generations.
metrics.currentValueContext: Set in device settings. Common values: 'NR/LTE/GSM/WCDMA' (auto), 'LTE only', 'NR only'.
metrics.healthyRange: Auto mode (NR/LTE/GSM/WCDMA) is best for most users.
metrics.commonCauses: User setting change, carrier provisioning, troubleshooting connectivity issues, developer options.

metrics.label: MSISDN (Phone Number)
metrics.whatItMeasures: Your mobile phone number associated with your SIM card — also called MSISDN in HSS terms.
metrics.currentValueContext: Read from SIM or network. NOTE: Most carriers no longer store this on the SIM, so it often shows as unavailable.
metrics.healthyRange: Any valid phone number is normal. 'N/A' is common on modern Android.
metrics.commonCauses: Carrier not writing MSISDN to SIM, Android 10+ privacy restrictions, multi-SIM configuration.
metrics.expansion: MOBILE STATION INTERNATIONAL SUBSCRIBER DIRECTORY NUMBER

metrics.label: IMSI
metrics.whatItMeasures: International Mobile Subscriber Identity — the unique global identifier for your SIM card's subscription.
metrics.currentValueContext: Only MCC-MNC prefix shown for privacy. Full IMSI requires privileged system API (denied on Android 10+).
metrics.healthyRange: Should start with your carrier's MCC-MNC. 'N/A' is normal on modern Android without root.
metrics.commonCauses: Android 10+ privacy restrictions (hidden API), privileged permission required, app not a system app.

metrics.label: SPN (Service Provider Name)
metrics.whatItMeasures: The service provider name stored on your SIM card — typically your carrier's branding name.
metrics.currentValueContext: Read directly from SIM card EF-SPN. This is the name your carrier wants displayed.
metrics.healthyRange: Any valid carrier name is normal.
metrics.commonCauses: Carrier branding on SIM, MVNO using host carrier name, carrier settings update.

metrics.label: Data Roaming
metrics.whatItMeasures: Whether your device has data roaming enabled — allowing mobile data while connected to a foreign network.
metrics.currentValueContext: ON = mobile data works while roaming. OFF = data disabled when roaming (WiFi only).
metrics.healthyRange: OFF is normal for domestic use to avoid charges. ON is needed when travelling abroad.
metrics.commonCauses: User setting in mobile network options, travel, carrier data roaming configuration.

metrics.label: Physical Cell ID (PCI)
metrics.whatItMeasures: The physical-layer identifier of the specific cell tower sector you are connected to (0-1007 for LTE, 0-1007 for NR).
metrics.currentValueContext: PCI is assigned by the network and re-used across towers — it identifies the sector, not the tower. Combined with Cell ID + TAC it uniquely locates the serving cell.
metrics.healthyRange: Any value 0-1007 is normal. Sudden changes mean you switched to a different sector or tower.
metrics.commonCauses: Tower handover, moving between sectors, carrier network configuration, new sites being added.

metrics.label: EARFCN
metrics.whatItMeasures: E-UTRA Absolute Radio Frequency Channel Number — the LTE channel number of the carrier your phone is camped on.
metrics.currentValueContext: A channel number, not a frequency. Convert to MHz via 3GPP 36.101 (100 kHz steps). Example: EARFCN 6300 → 806 MHz (Band 20).
metrics.healthyRange: Valid EARFCN 0-262143. Value maps directly to the LTE band table.
metrics.commonCauses: Determined by the serving network — changes when you switch bands or towers.
metrics.expansion: E-UTRA ABSOLUTE RADIO FREQUENCY CHANNEL NUMBER

metrics.label: NR-ARFCN
metrics.whatItMeasures: NR Absolute Radio Frequency Channel Number — the 5G channel number of the NR carrier (FR1 or FR2) your phone is using.
metrics.currentValueContext: Maps to 5G frequency via 3GPP 38.101. FR1 uses 5 kHz steps, FR2 uses 60 kHz. Example: n78 ARFCN 623334 → ~3.3 GHz.
metrics.healthyRange: Valid range 0-3279165. Value maps to the NR band table (n1, n41, n77, n78, n79, n258...).
metrics.commonCauses: Determined by the serving 5G network — changes when 5G band changes or during NSA/SA transitions.
metrics.expansion: NEW RADIO ABSOLUTE RADIO FREQUENCY CHANNEL NUMBER

metrics.label: Channel Bandwidth
metrics.whatItMeasures: The width of the radio channel your phone is using for the connected LTE cell — wider channels carry more data.
metrics.currentValueContext: Shown in MHz. Common LTE values: 1.4, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20 MHz. NR: 5, 10, 15, 20, 50, 100 MHz.
metrics.healthyRange: 10-20 MHz for LTE, 50-100 MHz for NR 5G is good. Narrower channels = slower speeds but better range.
metrics.commonCauses: Network configuration, congestion management, carrier aggregation state, rural vs urban deployment.

metrics.label: SS-RSRP (5G)
metrics.whatItMeasures: Synchronization Signal Reference Signal Received Power — the strength of the 5G NR signal, measured on the SSB (synchronization block).
metrics.currentValueContext: Measured in dBm. The 5G equivalent of LTE RSRP. Shown when the phone reports NR serving signal quality.
metrics.healthyRange: -80 dBm to -100 dBm is good. Below -120 dBm is very weak.
metrics.commonCauses: Distance from 5G tower, building penetration, mmWave blockers (n258+), carrier 5G deployment.
metrics.expansion: SYNCHRONIZATION SIGNAL REFERENCE SIGNAL RECEIVED POWER

metrics.label: C/N₀ (Carrier-to-Noise)
metrics.whatItMeasures: Carrier-to-Noise density ratio for each GNSS satellite — the strength of the satellite signal your phone's receiver sees.
metrics.currentValueContext: Measured in dB-Hz. Higher = stronger satellite signal. Peak value across all visible satellites is shown, plus per-constellation summaries.
metrics.healthyRange: Above 40 dB-Hz = strong. 25-40 dB-Hz = usable for positioning. Below 25 dB-Hz = marginal (urban canyons, indoors).
metrics.commonCauses: Satellite elevation, sky view obstruction (buildings/trees), antenna quality, ionosphere/troposphere effects, multipath reflections.

metrics.label: GNSS Fix
metrics.whatItMeasures: Global Navigation Satellite System status — whether your phone has a satellite position fix, how many satellites are visible, and which are contributing to the fix.
metrics.currentValueContext: Visible = satellites the receiver can track. In Fix = satellites actually used to compute your position. A fix needs at least 4 satellites in good geometry.
metrics.healthyRange: A fix with 6+ satellites used in fix is normal outdoors. 'Searching' indoors or with location disabled.
metrics.commonCauses: Being indoors/underground, airplane mode, location permission denied, GPS hardware state, satellite geometry in urban canyons.
